source_caption:
When Meryl Streep first sat down for the table read of The Devil Wears Prada, the cast fully expected her to deliver Miranda Priestly’s lines with a booming, imperious authority. Instead, Streep shocked the room by speaking in a faint, barely audible whisper—a brilliant, calculated choice she explicitly modeled after actor-director Clint Eastwood. She had previously noticed that Eastwood never raised his voice on set, forcing everyone to lean in and hang on his every word, automatically granting him the most power in the room. This soft-spoken delivery completely subverted the stereotypical “screaming boss” trope, making the character far more terrifying and requiring the production’s sound mixers to completely adjust their boom mic placements to capture her icy, subdued dialogue.

The Devil Wears Prada (2006), directed by David Frankel, starring Meryl Streep, Anne Hathaway, Emily Blunt, Stanley Tucci. A naive, newly graduated journalism student scores a coveted job as the assistant to a ruthless and demanding fashion magazine editor, forcing her to overhaul her entire identity to survive the cutthroat industry.

source_details.synopsis: The Devil Wears Prada is a 2006 American comedy-drama film directed by David Frankel and produced by Wendy Finerman. The screenplay, written by Aline Brosh McKenna, is based on the 2003 novel by Lauren Weisberger. The film stars Meryl Streep, Anne Hathaway, Stanley Tucci, and Emily Blunt. It follows Andy Sachs (Hathaway), an aspiring journalist who gets a job at a fashion magazine but finds herself at the mercy of her demanding editor, Miranda Priestly (Streep). 20th Century Fox bought the rights to a film adaptation of Weisberger's novel in 2003, before it was completed, but the project was not greenlit until Streep was cast. Principal photography lasted 57 days across September to December
